subject: Opportunistic prewarm lanes and throttle rules — TidalTech Dedicated
messages:
From: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@tidaltech.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@tidaltech.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Hi Tessa,

Quick question as we finalize the Dedicated contract: our traffic pattern has predictable daily spikes (2x baseline for ~40 minutes) plus occasional marketing-driven 6x spikes that last 20–45 minutes. We want to avoid tail latency for the user-facing routes but aren’t ready to commit to a much larger reserved pool across the board.

Can Redwood support an approach where a small reserved shoulder is combined with an "opportunistic prewarm" pool that we pay for on consumption (credits), plus an autoscale throttle to prevent noisy neighbors from collapsing the pool? Specifically:
- Prewarm lanes that are kept hot for short windows (10–60 mins) and drained afterward
- A burst credit model for marketing spikes (one-off top-ups)
- Clear eviction/throttle rules when cluster contention is high

Attaching our proposed SLA redline for reference. Can you share an ops-level playbook and a cost example for the above?

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
TidalTech
Attachment: TidalTech_SLA_draft_v3.pdf

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@tidaltech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Alex — thanks for the details and the SLA redlines, very helpful. Short answer: yes, we can support that pattern. Below is a high-level ops + commercial proposal; Karthik and Ben are looped for technical sizing and commercial terms respectively.

Proposal (summary):
1) Baseline reserved slab sized to 1.2x your 95th percentile baseline (keeps steady latency low).
2) Opportunistic prewarm lanes: a small set of warmable GPU instances (ephemeral) that are charged on a time-window basis and billed via burst credits when used. Lanes can be scheduled or invoked on demand with a minimum 10-minute keepalive.
3) Burst credit buckets: monthly rollover credits plus one-off top-ups for campaign spikes. We can offer tiered credit pricing (discounted for committed monthly spend).
4) Autoscale throttles & eviction policy: priority weighting by route + graceful eviction with KV cache spillback to cheaper instances and fallback to a smaller hosted model for non-critical traffic.

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Ops Playbook for prewarm lanes (start/stop sequences, cache warm strategies, metrics to watch) — doc attached (ops-playbook-opportunistic-lanes-v1.docx)
- Cost model (prewarm-cost-model.xlsx) showing burn rates for 10/30/60 minute windows
- SLA language we can commit to with clear definitions for prewarm availability, eviction windows and crediting mechanics

Next steps:
- Karthik: can you validate the sizing assumptions (GPU types, prewarm keepalive, KV warm-up times) and propose a minimal warm lane topology?
- Ben: pls propose the credit tiers and an interim commercial structure we can present to Procurement.

I’ll also propose a pilot window (2 weeks) where we enable a small opportunistic lane for a controlled campaign to validate run-rate and latency.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@tidaltech.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Alex / Tessa — technical notes based on their traffic profile: 

Sizing assumptions:
- Baseline: assume 8 A100-equivalent GPU slots for sustained baseline (we’ll verify once we see token/sec). 95th percentile multiplier: 1.2x -> reserve 10 slots.
- Prewarm lanes: implement 3 small lanes (each 0.5 GPU equivalent using multi-tenant vGPU packing) to start. Each lane supports quick cold-to-warm in ~45s for model weights + ~90s for KV warm-up to reach 95% steady state (depends on prompt fan-out).

Warm strategies and throttles:
- Keepalive: 10 minute minimum billing window per lane; extend automatically in 5 minute increments while sustained traffic > 20% of lane capacity.
- Eviction policy: Lanes are marked for eviction at 80% cluster pressure; eviction order: least-recently-used lane -> lanes with lowest priority tag -> opportunistic lanes used < 3x in last 24h. Evicted lanes persist KV cache snapshot for fast recovery (best-effort).
- Protective throttles: Per-route weightings; burst queue depth limit (max concurrent requests before 429) set per route; graceful degrade to a smaller hosted variant (e.g., 4-bit quantized model) for non-critical calls.

Operational telemetry we recommend monitoring during pilot:
- Lane spin-up latency distribution (P50/P95/P99)
- KV cache hit ratio during spin-up windows
- Credit burn per window and forecasted run rate
- Eviction triggers and time-to-recover after eviction

I’ll attach a quick reference diagram in the ops playbook. If TidalTech wants shorter warm times, we can pre-pull weights to a warm cache in exchange for longer minimum keepalive or higher monthly committed hours.

Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@tidaltech.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@tidaltech.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Alex / Procurement — commercial framing:

We can structure the commercial piece as follows:
- Committed reserved slab (monthly) priced per-GPU.
- Opportunistic prewarm lanes charged by minute with a 10-minute minimum, consumed from a burst-credit bucket. Burst credits are refillable monthly; unused credits roll over once per quarter (one rollover).
- One-off campaign top-ups: Procurement can purchase additional credit bundles at a premium price (we’ll provide a price sheet).
- Credit refunds / rebates: if we fail to meet prewarm availability SLA for a given month, we’ll refund credits proportionally for minutes lost (SLA formula to be added to the SOW).

Ben will attach a sample price sheet and an example invoice cadence. For the pilot we can offer a promotional rate on credit pricing for one month to gather real usage.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: prewarm-price-sheet.pdf (sent in a separate email)

From: Avery Collins <avery@tidaltech.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@tidaltech.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Thanks — a few procurement items and redlines from our legal/ops team after reviewing the ops playbook and SLA draft:
- We need a clear maximum eviction window (we propose 7 minutes from eviction trigger to throttle cut) or explicit credits for extended evictions.
- Prewarm credit accounting needs to show per-lane minute granularity in the billing export (csv) for auditability.
- For the pilot, TidalTech requires an option to cap total daily credit spend (hard cap) to avoid runaway marketing spends.

Attached is a redlined SLA with those asks. Also requesting an example of lane spin-up P95 from your pilot customers if available.

Attachment: TidalTech_SLA_draft_v3.pdf (redlined)

Regards,
Avery Collins
Head of Procurement, TidalTech

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery@tidaltech.ai>, Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@tidaltech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — handling periodic spikes & warmup options

Avery — thanks for the redlines, they’re reasonable. Confirmations and next actions: 
1) Eviction window: we can commit to an operational objective of 7 minutes from trigger to throttle enforcement for opportunistic lanes. If we exceed that bound we will credit prewarm minutes at 2x for the affected window (SOW language to reflect this escalation path).
2) Billing exports: we’ll provide per-lane minute granularity CSVs and a daily spend cap feature for the pilot (hard cap can be set by Procurement UI + alerts).
3) P95 spin-up: we’ll share anonymized spin-up P95s from comparable pilots (we’ve attached a summarized PDF) and include the spin-up P95 in the pilot acceptance criteria.

Next steps:
- I’ll circulate an updated SOW with the eviction-credit formula and billing export schema by EOD Thursday.
- Ben: please finalize the pilot credit pricing and promo rate.
- Karthik / Neha: standby to enable a 14-day pilot starting next Tuesday; we’ll provision 3 prewarm lanes and a hard credit cap as requested.

Thanks everyone — we’ll follow up with the SOW and the pilot enablement checklist.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ops-playbook-opportunistic-lanes-v1.docx; prewarm-cost-model.xlsx
